blocks.text: These appendices are the reference part of the report. They list the model files, the key parameter values, the RC channel map, the MCU mode logic, the main buses, the terms used in the report and the sources. All values were read from the repository on 2026-10-23: parameters from `params/param_<domain>.m`, interfaces from `docs/icd.md`, firmware logic from the MATLAB functions in `subsystems/`. The parameter files are the single source of truth. `shaddad_params` rebuilds `P`, `Ts`, `P_meta` and the `VC_*` variables every time the project opens, so if a value in this appendix and a file disagree, the file is correct.
Model and file map

The digital twin is the MATLAB project `Shaddad_UGV.prj`. The folder layout is shown in {fig:F33_project_structure.png} and summarised in {tab:tab_folders_arch} ({sec:ch02_architecture/Project and file structure}). Every `.slx` file is generated by a build script in `scripts/build/` from the parameter and bus definitions. Nobody edits a model by hand: to change a model, change its build script or a parameter file and regenerate the file. The build scripts are idempotent: each one closes, deletes and recreates its files.
Models

`models/` holds eight models. Phase 1 uses the top model and the three Model blocks inside it (MCU, BMS, Plant), all in Normal simulation mode. The four Phase 2 models sit behind `GNC_Variant` and become active only with `VC_PHASE` = 2. {tab:tab_app_models} lists them.

blocks.text: The variant controls and their defaults are listed in {tab:tab_vc_arch}. The scenario scripts set them per run through `Simulink.SimulationInput` (`scn_base_input`) and leave the base workspace unchanged.
RC channel map

The default transmitter is a RadioMaster TX16S in Mode 2 with a FrSky Archer SR10 receiver (`P.rc`). The channel assignment is a parameter (`P.rc.ch_map`, identical to `P.electronics.rcmap.ch`) and is never wired into a block diagram. The receiver failsafe presets are `P.rc.failsafe_raw`.

The channel map with the transmitter controls, the MCU decoding and the receiver failsafe presets is {tab:tab_rc_map} ({sec:ch06_electronics/RC Channel Map}); the stick and switch decoding is in {sec:ch06_electronics/RC Mapping}.

Decoding rules of `fw_rc_mapping` (Task_10): a stick channel is normalised as x = sat((raw - 992)/819.5, -1, 1). A 3-position switch decodes to position 1 + (x > -0.5) + (x > 0.5). A 2-position switch is ON when x > 0. The mode manager uses the RC inputs only while `rc_ok` is true (link not lost and no failsafe); otherwise it holds the last good values, so a failsafe preset never acts as a command. The remote E-stop on CH12 is evaluated only on frames with failsafe = 0 and frame_lost = 0.

The SBUS frame layout is {tab:tab_sbus_frame} and the line parameters are {tab:tab_sbus_line}; `sbus_frame_sync.m` accepts a frame only under the conditions listed in {sec:ch06_electronics/SBUS Decoder}.

The receiver switches to failsafe only after 1.0 s of continuous RF loss, but the MCU detects the loss much earlier: `rc_age` exceeds 0.10 s (about 7 frames) and RC_LINK_LOST starts a controlled stop. The remote E-stop is never inferred from a failsafe frame, because the CH12 preset is RUN (D34).
MCU modes and transitions

The mode manager runs in Task_10 (10 ms) as the MATLAB function `subsystems/electronics/mcu_mode_manager.m`. Its states are the `ShaddadMode` codes, and all its timers count 10 ms ticks. {tab:tab_app_modes} describes each mode with its beacon and buzzer pattern. The transitions in the priority order of the code are {tab:tab_modes} and the supervisor fault bits that drive them are {tab:tab_fault_bits} ({sec:ch06_electronics/Mode Manager} and {sec:ch06_electronics/Safety Supervisor and Watchdog}).

blocks.text: Three rules apply in every state. A new arm edge (CH6 off, then on) is needed after every stop before the robot moves again. Every reset edge re-issues the DO1 re-arm pulse, so the safety relay can close again. The mode manager requests HV from the BMS in every state except BOOT and FAULT while the key is on and no class A fault is active.

Class A removes torque at once (ESC disable). Class B starts a controlled stop at 1.0 m/s² and then returns to STANDBY. Class C derates or inhibits. Bits 0, 27, 29 and 31 are consequences of the hardware safety chain: they stop the robot but do not drop DO0, otherwise the E-stop loop could never close again (D30). Measured in Phase 1: BOOT -> SELFTEST -> STANDBY at 1.01 s and MANUAL at 2.04 s (D1); after the front E-stop in S8a, STO acts within 15 ms and the HW_ESTOP bit within 8 ms.
Bus overview

Every Model-block root port and the main subsystem interfaces are nonvirtual buses defined by `Simulink.Bus` objects. Unit-level firmware signals inside the models (for example `mode`, `cmd_src` and `drive_enable` from the mode manager) are scalars, and the Simscape physical connections are listed in docs/icd.md section 2. The 88 `Bus_*` objects are defined in `buses/buses_<domain>.m` and created by `shaddad_buses` at project startup (see {tab:tab_buses}). The element tables, with units, ranges and descriptions, are generated into docs/icd.md section 10. {tab:tab_app_buses} lists the buses that carry the Phase 1 signal chain. Phase 2 adds `Bus_McuStatus`, `Bus_GncCmd`, `Bus_NavState`, `Bus_Perception` and the GNC internal buses.

items: Futaba S.BUS serial protocol, as implemented by FrSky receivers (default receiver FrSky Archer SR10 in `P.rc`).
